description:
Curated worked-example repositories. This file is the trust root, on the same terms as widgets/packs.json: an example is admitted only at a full commit SHA, only from a curated owner, and every file it may fetch is pinned by digest here. A branch is never fetched, because a digest pinned against a moving ref verifies nothing.

An example is a RESOURCE -- a workflow document, data and a provenance record -- and declares no node type, so runtimeFetching: "none" in widgets/packs.json does not reach it. That rule governs widget definitions. See docs/experiments/127-examples-as-repositories.md.

governance.fetchPolicy: Only on an explicit practitioner action, never on load. Opening an example tells a server it was opened, which is the same disclosure the basemaps and Overpass make, and it is named in the interface and recorded in the receipt.
governance.verification: Every fetched file is digested with SubtleCrypto and compared to this catalog. A mismatch is a refusal, not a warning.
governance.offline: An example opened once is cached and stays available. Until it is opened it is FETCHABLE rather than AVAILABLE, and the interface must say which.

examples.title: Snow's South London water supply study, 1854

licence.data: CC0-1.0, except geo/sub-districts-csds.geojson which is BSD-2-Clause and geo/thames-reaches.geojson and geo/thames-tidal-limit.geojson which are ODbL-1.0
licence.source: Public domain. John Snow, On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, 1855.
licence.note: Why this is recorded per example rather than assumed: the mechanism exists so an example may carry terms this project could not adopt. Here the terms are none, because the figures were transcribed from an 1855 publication rather than from HistData (GPL) or causaldata (MIT). One file is an exception and is named in the licence field: the sub-district polygons are redistributed under BSD-2-Clause, which asks for attribution and does not restrict who may receive a map derived from them. That is why this example can carry them where the UK Data Service's sub-district shapefile, whose licence reaches derived datasets, could not be carried by anyone. A second exception was added on 2026-10-28 and it is the first SHARE-ALIKE one: the two Thames files are derived from OpenStreetMap, so a Derivative Database of them must be offered under the ODbL and a Produced Work must credit the contributors. That reaches only those two files -- they are additions beside the CC0 content, neither derived from it nor it from them -- which is why this example can still be used by a project under any licence, as long as it carries OpenStreetMap’s notice with the river.

examples.description: An investigation and its questions. Deaths per 1,000 people across the 32 sub-districts behind Snow's Table IX, the boundaries themselves as a 33-part study area with every part named, and 1849 against 1854 across Lambeth moving its intake upstream. Four transcribed tables, a georeferenced plate and three traced supply zones, with the terms of each.
examples.notYet: The three traced supply zones in geo/ are still for other tools: nothing in Fieldwork reads map2-water-supply-zones.geojson onto a canvas. geo/thames-tidal-limit.geojson is unread for a different reason -- it is a LineString, and no widget takes a line as a layer, so the limit ships as a file and is drawn by nothing. Everything else is live: the figures, the boundaries, the choropleth -- the 32 rates land on the 33 named parts through join_table_to_area -- the two Thames reaches through polygon_input, and Snow's Map 2 through map_image_input, both as ground under the choropleth and as a figure of its own.

notYetCorrected.was: Nothing joins a table to the parts of a study area, so the 32 mortality rates and the 32 named boundaries cannot colour one another. That join is the choropleth this example argues for in prose.
notYetCorrected.why: That sentence was true when the pin was written and false from 2026-10-25, when join_table_to_area shipped and the bundle gained a working choropleth workflow. The example repository corrected its own README the same day -- it says "Both are now false" and keeps the old sentence as the record of what the join was built to close -- and this field did not. THIS FIELD IS THE ONE A READER SEES: renderExampleCatalog prints it as "Not yet: ..." on the catalog card, so the deployed application advertised the example as missing the very workflow it ships. Found 2026-10-27 while asking what was left of the join work.

notYetCorrected.was: The georeferenced plate and the three traced supply zones in geo/ are still for other tools: nothing in Fieldwork reads a raster plate or those zones onto a canvas.
notYetCorrected.why: The plate half was true when the pin was written and false from 2026-10-27, when map_image_input shipped and the bundle wired Map 2 as ground under the choropleth. This is the SECOND time this field has advertised the example as missing a workflow it ships, and the second time it was found by somebody working on the thing rather than by a check -- the bundle is verified byte for byte and this sentence is verified by nobody. Found 2026-10-31 while giving the plate a workflow of its own. The zones half is still true and stays.

examples.usesNote: The node types the pinned bundle's workflows instantiate, DECLARED HERE rather than read from the clone, so widgets/evidence.json is the same on a machine that has the checkout and one that does not. A generated ledger whose value depends on what somebody happens to have cloned is not a measurement. validate:examples recomputes this list from the bundle wherever the checkout exists and refuses on a difference, so the declaration cannot drift from the bytes it describes.
examples.plateNote: geo/map2-ucla.jpg is pinned at 46,067,475 bytes: UCLA's full-resolution scan of Map 2, 12,828 x 10,097 pixels, and the plate all three workflows that draw Map 2 use. It is fetched only when one of them first runs, or when the learner asks for it in Configure..., and kept on the device after that. It replaced geo/map2.jpg (1,002 x 788) on 2026-11-28. The practitioner: "the original one was blurry when zoomed in and I could not read anything at all." Until then this note argued that the small plate was enough because a figure at screen size could not show more; that held for a figure seen whole and not for a plate read zoomed in. geo/map2-large.jpg (5,341,773 bytes) is still not pinned: nothing reads it.

examples.title: The Oswego church supper, 1940

licence.data: Stated as unconfirmed public domain for the line list; geo/lycoming-church.geojson is ODbL-1.0; the arrangement is CC0-1.0
licence.source: CDC Case Studies in Applied Epidemiology No. 401-303, which carries no copyright notice that was found.
licence.note: No explicit public-domain statement was read for the CDC guide, so this is a reasonable reading and not a confirmed fact.

examples.description: A person-level line list of 75 people and 14 foods: attack rates by food; when they fell ill, by the hour; hours from the meal to onset; who fell ill, by age and sex; the vanilla ice cream on its own; and a locator map of Lycoming in New York State, whose church is placed by inference. No study design is declared.
examples.notYet: No epidemic curve or incubation period: onset times are text here.

examples.title: DTP coverage and zero-dose children in Nigeria, 2024

licence.source: WorldPop, Modelled vaccination coverage and zero-dose estimates for Nigeria, 2000-2024, version 1.0. doi:10.5258/SOTON/WP00880
licence.note: Stated on the WorldPop dataset page. Attribution is required and is in NOTICE.txt. Boundaries were not reviewed separately.

examples.description: Five questions about 774 LGAs from modelled estimates: lowest coverage, highest burden, change over 20 years, and an illustrative rule over both values.
examples.notYet: Coverage intervals do not reach a map or a rule. Persistence, facilities, access and measles are not built.

examples.title: Salmonella Braenderup and melons, Germany 2021

licence.source: Łuczyńska et al., dataset on Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.7333295
licence.note: Stated on the Zenodo record. Attribution is in NOTICE.txt. The boundaries are © GeoBasis-DE / BKG, dl-de/by-2-0, via geoBoundaries.

examples.description: A case-control study with two control groups: 32 cases against 110 classical controls and against 81 matched panel controls, six melon items each, with a declared case-control design so only odds ratios are reported; who the cases were, all 34 fruit items, where the cases shopped, and where they lived over Germany's 16 Länder.
examples.notYet: The paper's multivariable model (Table 4) came from stepwise selection, which is not reproduced; its single-food adjusted ratios are.

examples.title: Ozone and child asthma emergency visits, New York City, 2016–2025

licence.source: Lian et al., Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.22757330; counts from NYC DOHMH EpiQuery
licence.note: The daily counts are fetched from the authors' Zenodo package when the example is opened and checked by digest. NYC.gov reserves all rights to them, so this repository holds none.

examples.description: Daily asthma emergency visits among children aged 5 to 17 in New York City with ozone, PM2.5 and weather, the tables fetched from where they are published. The June 2023 smoke days, ten years of daily visits, visits with ozone, PM2.5 and temperature in aligned panels, the authors' ozone model, a study-area map of the five boroughs and six ozone monitors for the Introduction, and Sentinel-5P NO₂ at the four NO₂ monitors beside their own readings.

examples.title: Dengue in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil, 2024

licence.source: Sánchez-Marqués and Sánchez, DATASET_MULTIMODAL_V8, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.22029053; counts from InfoDengue; boundaries from geoBoundaries (IBGE), CC BY 3.0 IGO
licence.note: Stated on the Zenodo record and by geoBoundaries. Attribution is in NOTICE.txt.

examples.description: Weekly notified dengue cases in the 92 municipalities of Rio de Janeiro state during Brazil's largest epidemic on record: the state's epidemic curve, notified cases per 100,000 residents by municipality on a map, and MODIS land surface temperature over each municipality for every 8-day period of 2024. A fourth workflow sets weekly cases beside the temperature 0 to 8 weeks earlier, in Poisson models drawn as a lag-response plot, with two leads as a falsification test. A fifth workflow widens it to 2010–2025, comparing weeks within a municipality, month and year and adjusting for rainfall.
examples.notYet: Vegetation (NDVI, EVI), a map of temperature by period, rainfall and humidity in the models, and errors allowing for week-to-week correlation.

examples.title: Rules on synthetic data

licence.source: Made up for this example; no person, place or count is real.
licence.note: Stated in the repository’s LICENSE. Every value is written in scripts/make-data.mjs.

examples.description: Seven questions on made-up data that exercise every feature of Apply ruleset: categories and values computed under conditions, a value read by a second rule, a setting with its unit, a division by zero, disagreeing rules, new cases from the previous row after a sort, rules the reasoner runs, rules over points on a map with counts stored as text, and a case definition in stages with is not and otherwise.
examples.notYet: Nothing on the list of Apply ruleset features is left unreached.

examples.title: Measles in Sierra Leone, 2019 to 2023

licence.data: Used with the Sierra Leone FETP’s agreement for distributable training materials; modified for a public teaching repository
licence.source: Sierra Leone Field Epidemiology Training Program, measles line list; de-identified and made semi-synthetic by the Fieldwork project
licence.note: Stated in the repository’s README and CITATION.cff, which credit both contributions. No row is a person; the file is not surveillance data.

examples.description: A semi-synthetic measles line list of 2,606 suspected cases: the epidemic curve by month of onset, the facilities that saw ten cases or more, found by name in GRID3’s register and mapped by band, and cases per 100,000 people by district over the 2021 census, on OCHA’s districts.
examples.notYet: The case classification by WHO’s definition, waiting on the FETP’s data dictionary.

examples.title: Sea-level rise at Manila’s health facilities

licence.data: Projections and sites CC BY 4.0, with three required citations; DeltaDTM v1.1 and DTU25MSS subsets CC BY 4.0; facilities retrieved from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0) by the workflows; the study area, diagram, manual and scripts CC0 1.0
licence.source: IPCC AR6 Sea Level Projections v20210809 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.5914709); DeltaDTM v1.1 (doi:10.4121/21997565); DTU25MSS (doi:10.11583/DTU.29412275); EGM2008 read from cdn.proj.org; OpenStreetMap via the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team export
licence.note: Stated in the repository’s README and CITATION.cff. The facilities file is a database derived from OpenStreetMap and offered under the ODbL.

examples.description: Published IPCC AR6 projections for eight Philippine tide gauges and 194 health facilities in coastal Manila: which gauge’s projection applies to each facility and how far it is, the rise there by 2100 under SSP2-4.5 with vertical land motion, 1,124 mm, and which facilities stand on ground below that projected level: 16 of 194, from DeltaDTM, EGM2008 and DTU25MSS, with no national datum. Not a flood model: its fourteen-note write-up opens with the vertical-datum diagram and says what the comparison leaves out.
examples.notYet: Not a flood model: no tide, surge, defences or drainage, and the open terrain model is least certain at the coast (about 0.45 m). NAMRIA’s mean sea level period remains unstated; the third workflow does without it.

examples.title: MERS-CoV, South Korea, 2015

licence.data: No licence stated for the data; used for teaching, as the outbreaks package describes it. The repository’s own files are CC0-1.0.
licence.source: The R package outbreaks (reconverse), mers_korea_2015, compiled by ECDC’s Epidemic Intelligence from public information in the outbreak’s first weeks.
licence.note: Decided 2026-11-11 by the practitioner: used in an example repository for teaching, attributed, never in the application.

examples.description: A line list of 162 cases, each case’s onset, diagnosis and report set against the 7-1-7 targets by a published ruleset and each verdict counted; and the 98 probable links, counted by source and by setting of exposure; and each hospital named for cases, placed and mapped over South Korea’s 17 provinces, coloured by its cases. Deaths by age class and by sex in a two-by-two; the days from exposure to onset, with its median by outcome, and from onset to death; and the secondary cases per source and the serial interval by setting; and how many each case infected, the offspring distribution; and each case its transmission chain, the epidemic curve by generation and the chains by size, and an inset over the hospitals at Pyeongtaek.
examples.notYet: No response dates, so no verdict on the third target.

examples.title: Population models beside a census

licence.data: Census counts: Statistics Botswana (free to use, acknowledged, as the user's own processing) and NISR (no terms found, used credited). Boundaries: geoBoundaries, CC BY 3.0 IGO (Botswana) and CC BY 4.0 (Rwanda). Rasters, read where published: WorldPop, GRID3 and GHS-POP, CC BY 4.0. The repository's own files are CC0-1.0.
licence.source: Statistics Botswana PHC 2022; NISR RPHC5 2022 Main Indicators; geoBoundaries 9469f09; WorldPop Global2 R2025A; GRID3 SSA 2025 v1.0; GHS-POP R2023A.
licence.note: NISR's counts used by the practitioner's decision of 2026-11-13, its terms unreadable; no raster is carried.

examples.description: WorldPop, GRID3 and GHS-POP totalled over each census district of Botswana (28) and Rwanda (30) and set beside the 2022 census as each district's share of the country: WorldPop and GRID3 follow the census by construction, GHS-POP does not.
examples.notYet: The rasters are not carried: each window is read again from the file downloaded from WorldPop, or from the JRC's copy for GHS-POP, and checked against its digest.

examples.title: Syndromic surveillance, 2026: a made-up district's emergency departments

licence.source: Made up for this example by scripts/make_visits.py
licence.note: No record describes a person; the district, its facilities and the outbreaks are invented. NSSP's definitions (credited, no licence stated), SNOMED CT identifiers (GPS, CC BY-ND 4.0) and ICD-11 codes (WHO, CC BY-ND 3.0 IGO) keep their owners' terms.

examples.description: 24,328 made-up emergency department visits over 25 weeks, each with its chief complaint and, for most, a discharge diagnosis in ICD-10, ICD-11 and SNOMED CT; a seeded norovirus outbreak among school-age children at one facility and a measles cluster. Visits sorted into syndromes by declared words and by four NSSP syndrome definitions, counted by day, and each day held to a threshold from its own past by CUSUM.
examples.notYet: No map: the visits carry no place. EARS C1 and C3 are compared in the README, not in a workflow.
